evals.prompt: Run a jobs-to-be-done (JTBD) framing on these three recruiting platforms before I write the vendor comparison.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Writes a solution-free job statement (verb + object + contextual clarifier) per option; Adds desired-outcome statements starting with minimize or increase; Lists competing solutions including an explicit non-consumption entry; Captures a struggling moment of 30 words or fewer with an evidence label.
expectations: Writes a solution-free job statement (verb + object + contextual clarifier) per option
Adds desired-outcome statements starting with minimize or increase
Lists competing solutions including an explicit non-consumption entry
Captures a struggling moment of 30 words or fewer with an evidence label

evals.prompt: Our tool comparison reads like a feature matrix — every vendor looks the same. Help me anchor it in what customers actually hire these products to do.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Diagnoses the comparison as tautological without a job statement; Produces one job statement per distinct job rather than one per vendor; Places each option against the job and the competing solution it displaces.
expectations: Diagnoses the comparison as tautological without a job statement
Produces one job statement per distinct job rather than one per vendor
Places each option against the job and the competing solution it displaces

evals.prompt: We're deciding between buying an internal-mobility platform, using LinkedIn Recruiter, or keeping our manual process. What job is each one hired for, and what does the customer do without any tool?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Names non-consumption (the manual status quo) as a competing solution; States the circumstance — segment, size, industry — that has the job; Notes where two options serve different jobs instead of ranking them on one list.
expectations: Names non-consumption (the manual status quo) as a competing solution
States the circumstance — segment, size, industry — that has the job
Notes where two options serve different jobs instead of ranking them on one list

evals.prompt: Write a job statement and desired outcome statements for a warehouse robotics buyer, with the competing solutions including non-consumption.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Uses Ulwick's outcome grammar: direction of improvement + metric + object of control + contextual clarifier; Keeps every statement free of product, vendor and feature nouns; Emits the output template with all mandatory fields filled.
expectations: Uses Ulwick's outcome grammar: direction of improvement + metric + object of control + contextual clarifier
Keeps every statement free of product, vendor and feature nouns
Emits the output template with all mandatory fields filled

evals.prompt: Place these five vendors on a 2x2 competitive landscape by price and integration depth — a magic-quadrant style map.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Does not write job or desired-outcome statements; Selects axes and places competitors on a 2x2 map (position-competitor behaviour).
expectations: Does not write job or desired-outcome statements
Selects axes and places competitors on a 2x2 map (position-competitor behaviour)

evals.prompt: Is generative AI for HR overhyped right now — where does it sit on the Gartner hype cycle?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Places the technology on a maturity curve rather than framing a customer job; Reports the hype-cycle stage with indicator evidence.
expectations: Places the technology on a maturity curve rather than framing a customer job
Reports the hype-cycle stage with indicator evidence
